question: How do soil temperature, soil water content and soil type (peat or mineral) relate to the CH4 and N2O fluxes at Anttila, Särkisuo and Viikki?

method.timeBase: local day = calendar day of ts_start + utc_offset_min (UTC+2); open finding ANT-01, SAR-01, VII-01: the true local day starts 2 h earlier
rules: Sites: Anttila (mineral soil), Sarkisuo (drained peat) and Viikki (clay loam, mineral). CH4
is only at Anttila and Sarkisuo (2022 to 2023), N2O at all three (Anttila and Sarkisuo 2022 to
2023, Viikki 2022 to 2025). The fluxes are the gap-filled values of the providers (the
database has no measured CH4 or N2O). The gap-fill models use soil drivers, thus a part of
each relation below comes from the models (circularity). Soil drivers: tsoil (degC) and swc
(m3 m-3) of the shallowest sensor (Anttila and Sarkisuo 5 cm, Shurpali et al. 2025 p. 4;
Viikki 14 cm). The soil type is static per site (LITERATURE). Units are the harmonised units:
ch4 umol CH4 m-2 s-1, n2o nmol N2O m-2 s-1 (positive = emission).
1. Local day = calendar day of ts_start + utc_offset_min. Daily mean of each variable; a day
keeps the mean of a variable when the variable has MIN_VALUES_PER_DAY (40) or more of the
48 half hours, else the daily value is missing. Each analysis uses the days where all its
variables have a daily value. For the text only, daily CH4 is also given in
mg CH4 m-2 d-1 and daily N2O in mg N2O m-2 d-1.
2. Temperature response, per site and gas: daily tsoil in 1 degC bins (bin = floor(tsoil));
a bin needs MIN_BIN_DAYS (10) days. Per bin: median and 25 and 75 % quantiles of the daily
flux. Spearman rho (scipy.stats.spearmanr) over all days. Exponential fit
F = F10 x Q10^((T - 10) / 10) to the bin medians that are > 0, at the bin centres. The
fit is in log space: ln F = ln F10 + k (T - 10) (scipy.optimize.curve_fit), Q10 =
exp(10 k). Thus each bin has the same relative weight; a fit in linear space lets one
warm bin with a fertilisation peak set the curve. The fit needs 5 or more such bins, and
they must be 75 % or more of the bins; else the fit is null with the reason. 95 % CI of
Q10 = exp(10 (k +/- t(0.975, n - 2) x SE(k))), n = number of bins. R2 is in log space.
"The bins" = the bins with MIN_BIN_DAYS or more days; bin centre = (floor(x / width) +
0.5) x width.
3. Water response: the same with swc in 0.02 m3 m-3 bins (bin = floor(swc / 0.02)), and
Spearman rho. No fit.
4. Joint effect, per site and gas: OLS of the daily flux on z(tsoil), z(swc) and
z(tsoil) x z(swc) (z = (x - mean) / SD of the days of the site and gas, SD with n - 1),
with a constant; the mean and SD come from the OLS days (days with flux, tsoil and swc).
Standard errors: Newey-West HAC with 7 lags (statsmodels: Bartlett kernel, no small-sample
correction; CI and p-values from the normal distribution). Reported: coefficients in flux
units per 1 SD, 95 % CI, p-values and R2.
5. Soil type, Sarkisuo (peat) against Anttila (mineral): (a) annual sums per site, local
year and gas = sum of the 30-min values x 1800 s, in kg CH4 ha-1 yr-1 and kg N2O ha-1
yr-1 (molar mass CH4 16.043, N2O 44.013 g mol-1), with the coverage (values / half hours
of the year); a year with coverage < 0.9 is partial. The 2022 sums are compared with
Shurpali et al. 2025 Table 3 (LITERATURE). (b) Paired days: the local days in 2022 and
2023 where both sites have a daily value of the gas. Daily distributions (median, 25 and
75 %) and the mean daily difference Sarkisuo - Anttila, with a 95 % CI from a block
bootstrap: the paired days in date order are cut into blocks of 7 days (BLOCK_DAYS); the
last, shorter block is kept. Each replicate draws as many blocks as there are, with
replacement (numpy.random.default_rng(BOOT_SEED), BOOT_REPS 5000); the statistic is the
mean of all days in the drawn blocks; percentile interval. Viikki gets annual sums too
(N2O). kg ha-1 = sum x 1800 s x 1e-6 (CH4) or 1e-9 (N2O) mol x molar mass g mol-1 x 10.
6. Sensitivity for N2O: steps 2 to 4 again without the days of fertilisation effect: the
local days 0 to 29 after each fertilisation event of db/events.parquet (the event day is
day 0; FERT_DAYS 30). Events: rows with type == 'fertilisation'. Also: the share of the
N2O sum of each site-year that is on these days = sum of the daily N2O means of the days
in the windows / sum of all daily N2O means of the year.
7. Heat map (Figure 3): mean daily flux per cell of 2 degC tsoil x 0.04 m3 m-3 swc
(cell = floor(tsoil / 2), floor(swc / 0.04)); a cell needs MIN_CELL_DAYS (5) days.
8. Each step that removes rows or days logs a count (results.json dataVersion.steps).
9. Open findings of docs/anomaly-data-report.md that touch this dive are printed
(OPEN_FINDINGS).
openFindings: Gap-filled fluxes (limit of the method): the database has only the gap-filled CH4 and N2O values. In 2022, 28 to 67 % of the 30-min values were measured (Shurpali 2025 p. 3). The gap-fill models use soil drivers, thus a part of each relation comes from the models.

ANT-01, SAR-01, VII-01 (open, waits for the providers): the raw stamps of Anttila, Sarkisuo and Viikki are UTC, but the build reads them as UTC+2. A local day of these sites thus holds the hours 02:00 to 02:00 true local time. Daily means change little; the annual sums change by the 2 hours at the ends of the year only.

VII-06 (open question): the Viikki N2O unit can be ug N2O or ug N2O-N. The build assumes ug N2O. If it is N2O-N, all Viikki N2O values are 1.57 times too small. The relations (rho) do not change; the Viikki slopes, sums and medians change by this factor.
SAR-07 (known): Sarkisuo CH4 and N2O start on 2022-05-06. The 2022 sums are partial years (coverage 0.66); the paired days of Sarkisuo and Anttila start on that day.

VII-04 (open, waits for the provider): the Viikki tsoil at 14 cm has spikes up to 28.9 degC after field work in May, August and September 2025. On 34 days the daily mean can be 2 to 5 degC too high; some of these days are in the 30 days after the fertilisation of 2025-05-10. The dive does not remove them.

SAR-04, ANT-05, VII-03 (zero curtain): in winter, tsoil stays near 0 degC for weeks (Sarkisuo 0.2 degC for most of the winter 2022-23; a sensor floor is an open question). The 0 degC bins thus hold many winter days with different fluxes.

fit.reason: bins with median > 0 are less than 75% of the bins

figures.title: Daily CH₄ and N₂O flux against the daily soil temperature at Anttila (mineral soil), Särkisuo (drained peat) and Viikki (clay loam): median per 1 °C bin with the 25 to 75 % band, and the Q₁₀ fit.
figures.desc: Two panels, one above the other: CH₄ flux (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, top) and N₂O flux (nmol m⁻² s⁻¹, bottom) against the daily mean soil temperature (°C, shared x axis; Anttila and Särkisuo at 5 cm, Viikki at 14 cm). Each line is the median of the daily means per 1 °C bin with the 25 to 75 % band; the dotted lines are Q₁₀ fits. CH₄: Anttila: ρ −0.06 (n = 724 days), tsoil −0.2 to 23.8 °C, largest bin median 0.000303 µmol CH₄ m⁻² s⁻¹ at 16.5 °C, no Q₁₀ fit (bins with median > 0 are less than 75% of the bins); Särkisuo: ρ 0.82 (n = 504 days), tsoil 0.2 to 19.1 °C, largest bin median 0.0730 µmol CH₄ m⁻² s⁻¹ at 13.5 °C, Q₁₀ 4.65 (95 % CI 2.50 to 8.64). N₂O: Anttila: ρ 0.17 (n = 724 days), tsoil −0.2 to 23.8 °C, largest bin median 0.282 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 18.5 °C, Q₁₀ 2.06 (95 % CI 1.40 to 3.03); Särkisuo: ρ 0.64 (n = 504 days), tsoil 0.2 to 19.1 °C, largest bin median 1.67 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 17.5 °C, Q₁₀ 3.25 (95 % CI 1.67 to 6.30); Viikki: ρ −0.07 (n = 1326 days), tsoil −2.4 to 22.4 °C, largest bin median 1.26 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 12.5 °C, Q₁₀ 0.91 (95 % CI 0.57 to 1.43). CH₄ against soil temperature: Anttila no clear monotonic relation; Särkisuo a strong positive relation. N₂O against soil temperature: Anttila a weak positive relation; Särkisuo a strong positive relation; Viikki no clear monotonic relation. The fluxes are gap-filled values. Flux > 0 = emission.

figures.title: Daily CH₄ and N₂O flux against the daily soil water content at Anttila (mineral soil), Särkisuo (drained peat) and Viikki (clay loam): median per 0.02 m³ m⁻³ bin with the 25 to 75 % band.
figures.desc: Two panels, one above the other: CH₄ flux (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, top) and N₂O flux (nmol m⁻² s⁻¹, bottom) against the daily mean soil water content (m³ m⁻³, shared x axis). Each line is the median of the daily means per 0.02 m³ m⁻³ bin with the 25 to 75 % band. CH₄: Anttila: ρ 0.03 (n = 724 days), swc 0.11 to 0.45 m³ m⁻³; Särkisuo: ρ 0.11 (n = 504 days), swc 0.29 to 0.80 m³ m⁻³. N₂O: Anttila: ρ −0.28 (n = 724 days), swc 0.11 to 0.45 m³ m⁻³; Särkisuo: ρ −0.30 (n = 504 days), swc 0.29 to 0.80 m³ m⁻³; Viikki: ρ 0.30 (n = 1294 days), swc 0.10 to 0.53 m³ m⁻³. CH₄ against soil water content: Anttila no clear monotonic relation; Särkisuo a weak positive relation. N₂O against soil water content: Anttila a weak negative relation; Särkisuo a weak negative relation; Viikki a weak positive relation. The fluxes are gap-filled values. Flux > 0 = emission.

figures.title: Mean daily CH₄ and N₂O flux per cell of soil temperature and soil water content, one panel per site and gas.
figures.desc: Five heat maps: x axis daily mean soil temperature (°C, −2 to 22), y axis daily mean soil water content (m³ m⁻³, 0.08 to 0.80), the same axes in all panels. Top row CH₄ at Anttila and Särkisuo (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹); bottom row N₂O at Anttila, Särkisuo and Viikki (nmol m⁻² s⁻¹). Cells of 2 °C by 0.04 m³ m⁻³ with 5 or more days; colour = mean daily flux, diverging around 0, each panel with its own colour scale. Anttila CH₄: 40 cells, 663 of 724 days; largest mean 0.00309 µmol CH₄ m⁻² s⁻¹ at 6 to 8 °C and 0.28 to 0.32 m³ m⁻³ (n = 5). Särkisuo CH₄: 29 cells, 375 of 504 days; largest mean 0.0836 µmol CH₄ m⁻² s⁻¹ at 12 to 14 °C and 0.76 to 0.80 m³ m⁻³ (n = 16). Anttila N₂O: 40 cells, 663 of 724 days; largest mean 0.884 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 16 to 18 °C and 0.28 to 0.32 m³ m⁻³ (n = 18). Särkisuo N₂O: 29 cells, 375 of 504 days; largest mean 6.08 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 12 to 14 °C and 0.36 to 0.40 m³ m⁻³ (n = 8). Viikki N₂O: 70 cells, 1216 of 1294 days; largest mean 5.44 nmol N₂O m⁻² s⁻¹ at 14 to 16 °C and 0.36 to 0.40 m³ m⁻³ (n = 10). Soil water ranges (m³ m⁻³): Anttila 0.11 to 0.45; Särkisuo 0.29 to 0.80; Viikki 0.10 to 0.53. Grey = no cell. The flux values are gap-filled. Flux > 0 = emission.

figures.title: Annual CH₄ and N₂O sums per site-year at the peat site Särkisuo and the mineral sites Anttila and Viikki, with the 2022 values of Shurpali et al. (2025).
figures.desc: Two bar charts of annual sums per site-year: CH₄ in kg CH₄ ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (left; Anttila and Särkisuo 2022 and 2023) and N₂O in kg N₂O ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (right; also Viikki 2022 to 2025). A lighter, hatched bar with an asterisk is a partial year (coverage below 90%). Black diamonds with a bar are the 2022 values and ranges of Shurpali et al. (2025) Table 3. CH₄: Anttila 2022 2.34; Anttila 2023 2.73; Särkisuo 2022 103 (partial, coverage 0.66); Särkisuo 2023 128. N₂O: Anttila 2022 3.85; Anttila 2023 1.70; Särkisuo 2022 16.0 (partial, coverage 0.66); Särkisuo 2023 11.3; Viikki 2022 16.8; Viikki 2023 5.56; Viikki 2024 4.58; Viikki 2025 6.43. Shurpali 2022 Anttila CH₄: 2.0 (2.0 to 3.0); this dive 2.34. Shurpali 2022 Särkisuo CH₄: 110 (110 to 120); this dive 103. Shurpali 2022 Anttila N₂O: 3.8 (3.7 to 4.0); this dive 3.85. Shurpali 2022 Särkisuo N₂O: 16 (16 to 17); this dive 16.0. Ratio Särkisuo / Anttila of the annual CH₄ sum: 2022 44, 2023 47 (Särkisuo 2022 is a partial year). Ratio Särkisuo / Anttila of the annual N₂O sum: 2022 4.2, 2023 6.6 (Särkisuo 2022 is a partial year). If the Viikki N₂O unit is N₂O-N (open finding VII-06, status: waits for provider), the Viikki bars are 1.57 times higher (2022: 26.3).
